newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends down about 1/4 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends down about 1/4 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended Thursday's session off about 1/4 point, avoiding somewhat steeper losses in the Treasury market.
The Treasury long bond lost 13/32 heading into the New York close, moving the yield to 7.05 percent.
In the muni secondary, bids on Chicago Board of Education MBIA 6.0s of 2026 were unchanged at 99-7/8. Alliance Airport Authority, Texas, 6-3/8s of 2021 were up 1/8 at 97-7/8.
Smith Barney Inc said it did not reprice Honolulu, Hawaii's $100 million general obligation bonds, which the firm priced at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2016. To see the
Bear Stearns & Co said it repriced $30 million Nevada Housing Division bonds, but left the top yield in 2028 unchanged at 6.35 percent. To see the repricing, double click on nN19175068.
In Thursday's economic data releases, a stronger-than-expected U.S. August housing starts report overshadowed a decline in weekly jobless claims.

August starts were the strongest since March 1994, rising 4.5 percent to an annual rate of 1.525 million units compared to the average trade estimate of 1.445 million units and against July's rate of 1.46 million units.
Jobless claims for the week ended Sept 14 fell to 329,000. Economists on average were looking for claims to fall to 335,000.
